title: Jean Cassidy:
headline: A first-time volunteer at the Sanctuary Golf Classic gives the Navy SEAL Foundation one word, heartwarming, then shows why the day is fun: golf, friends and a good cause.
story: Jean volunteered at the Sanctuary Golf Classic (25 June 2026, Sedalia, Colorado). The crew asked every guest the same three questions: describe the Navy SEAL Foundation in one word, why do you keep coming back, and your best golf tip. The cut keeps her answers in that order.

The turn: asked why she keeps coming back, she says it is her first time. Then the why: her son is in the military, golf is fun, and it is all for a good cause. Loose and warm, the way NSF wants donor and volunteer clips. Every answer has its question on screen, so the viewer always knows what she is answering.
do: Open on Jean already saying <q>It's heartwarming</q>, with the question on screen at 0:00.
Put each question on screen as top text when she answers it.
Swap the drink and food shots: the man raising his drink under <q>Bloody Marys</q>, the table of food under <q>eating great food</q>.
Hold the last frame to the end. The video never ends on black.
Use the NSF fonts on every super and text: Oswald and Open Sans.
dont: No fade to black at the end. The thumbnail and the loop point land on the last frame.
No one in uniform in any B-roll shot.
Do not use the crew talk at 02:03 to 02:13 (<q>that's not a really good one</q>).
Never write Navy SEAL Foundation without <q>the</q>. SEAL always in capitals.

NSF has no graphics package yet. Use the MG library on this page (NSF colours and fonts from navysealfoundation.org).
Warm, light, modern, no lyrics. No campy stings.
tech: Vertical 2160×3840, about 29.97 fps (visual.json). The interview file on Drive has no extension; add .mov if your NLE needs it. B-roll IMG files are vertical 2160×3840 too.
All clips are vertical. No crop. Reframing from the 4K source is safe up to about 200 percent.
Check by ear which track carries her mic. NSF rule: a little noise is fine. Do not over-clean with AI tools, it hurts the voice.
-14 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP peak. Music under the voice.
Burned in on every spoken line. White Open Sans Bold on the NSF blue box #003C69, low in the frame, one line at a time. SEAL in capitals and singular; always the Navy SEAL Foundation.
Hold the last frame. No fade to black (V1 ended on 0.13 s of black).
H.264 MP4, 1080×1920, 9:16. Upload to Frame.io with the file name under the title, then Ready for Review.
checklist: Frame 1 is Jean saying <q>heartwarming</q> with the question already on screen. No logo, name or fade.
The question text does not animate on at 0:00.
Name super at 00:06, 2 s: Jean Cassidy / Volunteer. Surname confirmed (see decisions).
Every answer has its question on screen: one word, coming back, golf tip.
The drink shot sits on <q>Bloody Marys</q> and the food shot on <q>eating great food</q>.
<q>and then if you're not moving,</q> runs as one caption line with the words before it, no full stop in the middle.
No one in uniform in any shot.
Captions: SEAL in capitals, <q>the Navy SEAL Foundation</q> with <q>the</q>, no typos.
The video ends on a held frame or the end card, never on black.

Atdhe asked on V2 (20 Oct): “is this the right font?” The client file names Oswald and Open Sans, the fonts on navysealfoundation.org. Chris texted a colour reference that is not in the client file. Atdhe: confirm the font and the colour reference.
